guard: a provider invalid_request during Jcode's mandatory readiness turn exposes only the safely classified provider code and rejected model/effort value; slow Jcode bootstrap receives its declared bounded manager readiness window rather than an early generic uncertainty verdict
command: pnpm smoke:jcode-host && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/core build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/workspace build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/connector-core build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/manager build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/cli build && pnpm smoke:readiness:live
completionMarker: provider readiness refusal names its code and rejected model parameter
why: #828 was measured at the readiness-turn boundary: a provider gateway rejected a model id, but
the operator saw only `startup failed (unknown)` and had to inspect private harness logs.
The host smoke drives the SDK event that JcodeClient.run turns into HarnessError and proves
the public line contains only the classified provider code and rejected model id.
#827 was measured as a Jcode seat joining minutes after the manager's generic 30s window.
The live readiness smoke runs an actual manager and child process: the child joins after a
shortened generic window but inside the connector-declared Jcode-shaped bound.
Each mutation removes one load-bearing behavior and names the assertion that must go red.

mutations.name: Jcode readiness refusal is collapsed back to unknown
mutations.replace: process.stderr.write(`[cotal-jcode] fatal: Jcode host startup failed (${startupFailureCode(error)}); inspect the private Jcode logs.\n`);
mutations.expectRed: provider readiness refusal names its code and rejected model parameter

mutations.name: Jcode no longer declares its long bounded bootstrap window
mutations.expectRed: declares a bounded three-minute bootstrap window
